rules.title: Berkeley ban on coordinated pricing algorithms for rents and occupancy
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use, and vendors may not sell or provide, coordinated pricing algorithms that use nonpublic competitor data to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. The City Attorney or an aggrieved tenant can sue, with civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation.
rules.key_value: ban on coordinated pricing algorithms using nonpublic competitor data (<90 days old); civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley
rules.effective_date_note: The ordinance excerpt in D001 states no effective date (passed to print Nov 18, 2025). March 1, 2026 is the date reported for the ordinance text; the law-firm alert D002/D037 says January 2026.
rules.exemptions: Excludes aggregated anonymous reports that do not recommend rents, affordable-housing rent/income limit products, and market research for financing, appraisal, or software development research/testing/training.
rules.penalty: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; damages, injunctive relief, restitution; each month and each unit is a separate violation; prevailing plaintiff gets attorney's fees
rules.conflict_note: Two published effective dates: March 1, 2026 (ordinance text, not shown in D001) vs. January 2026 (Morgan Lewis alert D002/D037).
rules.review_note: Alert also notes RealPage v. City of Berkeley was voluntarily dismissed with prejudice Jan. 14, 2026.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords may not ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or lease decisions, and must give written notice and a chance to respond before taking any action based on criminal history.
rules.key_value: ban on criminal-history inquiries and use in tenant selection
citation_aliases: Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making
rules.effective_date_note: Council passed the ordinance April 14, 2020; the document does not state the effective date.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit; units rented under an agreement allowing owners to move back (BMC 13.76.130 A.9); existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of $1,000 to $10,000 per violation, actual damages or three times one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.

unverifiable_exemptions: existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance – just cause eviction, notice rules and relocation assistance (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered units can be evicted only for just cause. A landlord cannot evict for nonpayment unless rent owed is at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent, nor for refusing to sign a new fixed-term lease. Termination notices must refer the tenant to the Rent Board and be filed with it within three business days. Owner move-in and Ellis Act evictions require relocation assistance ($19,413 standard plus $6,471 for qualifying households in 2026).
rules.key_value: Nonpayment eviction only if debt ≥ 1 month HUD FMR; 2026 relocation $19,413 + $6,471
citation_aliases: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value
rules.effective_date_note: Measure BB passed Nov 2024; Notice of Tenant Rights applies to tenancies started on or after 2024-12-20; 2026 relocation amounts effective 2026-01-01.
rules.exemptions: Exempt: golden duplexes, owner-shared kitchen/bath units, certain ADU properties, university housing, nonprofit cooperatives.
rules.review_note: Chapter number 13.76 is not stated in the coverage or relocation documents; inferred from references to BMC 13.76.110A and 13.76.130 in other Berkeley documents.

unverifiable_exemptions: unit shared with landlord who lived there first

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee disclosure and ban on non-refundable renewal fees
rules.requirement: Owners who charge a credit-report/application fee must give applicants a Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and the maximum fee cap under Civ. Code 1950.6(b) before taking the fee (2026 cap $68.96). Landlords cannot charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy or add or replace a roommate.
rules.key_value: Disclosure of fee rights and cap before fee; no non-refundable renewal/roommate fees
rules.quoted_span: the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance – Annual General Adjustment (max 5%, Measure BB)
rules.requirement: For fully covered units, yearly rent increases are limited to the Annual General Adjustment set by the Rent Board (65% of CPI), which can never exceed 5%. The 2026 AGA is 1.0%. Banked unused AGAs may still be used to reach the rent ceiling. Newer buildings, most condos and single-family homes are not rent controlled.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%
rules.effective_date_note: Measure BB cap passed Nov 2024; no exact start date stated. 2026 AGA effective no earlier than 2026-01-01.
rules.coverage_conditions: Fully covered: most multifamily units built before 1980, single-family homes with tenancies begun before 1996, rooming houses.
rules.exemptions: Partially covered/exempt units (new construction with CO after June 1980, most condos, single-family tenancies from 1996, certain subsidized units) have no rent ceiling; 2026 AGA does not adjust Costa-Hawkins-set rents for tenancies beginning on or after 2025-01-01.
rules.conflict_note: Cutoff stated variously as 'built before 1980' (D006, D009) and 'CO after June 1980' (D009); June 30, 1980 used. State Costa-Hawkins limits local rent control for newer buildings and single-family homes/condos.
rules.review_note: Chapter 13.76 inferred from the reference to BMC 13.76.110A in D008.

rules.title: Berkeley security deposit interest requirement
rules.requirement: For units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on security deposits at the end of each year, with a prorated amount if the tenant moves out earlier. The deposit cap itself comes from state law.
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year
rules.coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.interaction: Operates alongside state cap in Civ. Code § 1950.5.
rules.review_note: Municipal code section not stated in the documents; ch. 13.76 inferred.

The Berkeley effective-date conflict (March 1, 2026 vs. January 2026) is noted on the algorithmic record. The 1980 rent-control cutoff is ambiguous and is noted on the rent record.
